```{r, setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(magrittr)
library(driveanalytics)

knitr::opts_knit$set(echo = FALSE)

# Get the render format
render_format <- knitr::opts_knit$get('rmarkdown.pandoc.to')
if (render_format == "") render_format <- "html"
```

## Overview
This method computes and plots how many unique events patients typically have, by cohort. This can be used to identify if cohorts are more or less complex than each other.

## Method
This method simply computes the number of unique events that occur for each patient in each cohort and aggregates these values into a table and histogram.

## Considerations and Limitations
* None

## Example
The following example shows the number of unique events that typically happen per patient in two cohorts.

The plot and table show the following information:

1. Cohort A typically has a lower number of events per patient than cohort B
1. The modal number of unique events per patient in cohort A is about 10 and in cohort B is about 20.
1. Two patients in cohort A and zero patients in cohort B had no events at all.
1. The maximum number of unique events per patient is 36, a patient from cohort B.

```{r, example, echo=FALSE, dpi=200, out.width="100%", fig.dim = c(8, 3)}

# Create a random sample of patients in two cohorts and assign random events
set.seed(123)
n <- 1000
nev <- n * 5
df_pde <- tibble::tibble(
  project_id = 1:n,
  cohort_id = project_id,
  cohort = sample(c("A","B"), n, replace = TRUE),
)
df_dia <- df_pde %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    nreps = pmax(dplyr::if_else(
      cohort == "A",
      as.integer(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 10, 4)),
      as.integer(rnorm(dplyr::n(), 20, 5))
    ), 0)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::slice(rep(seq(dplyr::n()), nreps)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(project_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(event = 1:dplyr::n()) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(project_id)

# Perform frequency analysis and get results
gec <- driveanalytics::gen_event_count(df_dia, df_pde, "event")
plot(gec)
tabulate(gec, render_format)

```
